records.body:
## Why a week with death

Every tradition in this directory keeps death in view, and none of them treats it as morbid. The Theravada monk recollects it with every breath. The Tibetan prepares for the bardo like packing for a journey. Advaita turns the question around: find who it is that is afraid. The Platonist practises dying.

The journey this essay accompanies does one talk and one practice a day for a week. That is deliberately light. The point is not to finish but to notice which day snags — grief, urgency, curiosity, resistance — and follow that thread into the topic hub.

Go gently; skip a day whenever you need to. The dead are in no hurry.
